articles.title: AI Chatbot Analytics: Measuring What Matters
articles.excerpt: You paid for a chatbot. It sits on your website, and every month someone sends you a report full of numbers. Conversations are up, messages are up, and everything looks like it is working. Support tic…
articles.body: You paid for a chatbot. It sits on your website, and every month someone sends you a report full of numbers. Conversations are up, messages are up, and everything looks like it is working. Support tickets have not fallen, leads have not risen, and nobody can say, with evidence, whether the chatbot earns its keep. Chatbot analytics are not hard. The hard part is knowing which numbers mean something and which are decoration. Measure the wrong things and you keep paying for a chatbot that looks busy and does nothing. Why most chatbot reports mislead you Most chatbot platforms ship a dashboard that looks impressive on day one: total conversations, total messages, average session length. They go up as soon as the chatbot goes live, and that feels like progress. It usually is not.
articles.author: Tjvex Studio

articles.body: On Wildberries, a listing can look fully in stock and still have one pair left in the size your customer wears. Take one pair of platform sneakers, product 152540730, with more than 150,000 ratings. On 20 November size 45 had 1 unit and size 43 had 42. On 28 November it was the other way round: size 43 had 1 unit and size 45 had 50. Size 46 showed 0 both times. Over the same eight days the price went from 1,340 to 1,245 RUB. A shopping agent that recommends this product in size 43 today is about to send someone to an empty shelf. A reseller who only checks the listing page misses the moment a competitor's size runs out. Both need stock per size. The product's own "in stock" flag stays true until the last size is gone. I built Wildberries Scraper on Apify for this.

articles.body: AI crawlers now visit most websites every day. Some collect pages to train models. Others fetch pages live so ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity can answer a user's question and cite you. That makes one small file very important: robots.txt . A single wrong line can either hand your content to every AI model or quietly remove your business from AI answers. This guide shows how a robots.txt AI block works, which bots matter, and how to choose what to block and what to allow.

articles.title: Google preannounced the December core update — use the warning to find your lost keywords
articles.excerpt: Google has never warned anyone about a core update before it started. On 24 November, it did. The November 2026 core update finished that morning. It began on 10 November at 10:06 US/Pacific and ended…
articles.body: Google has never warned anyone about a core update before it started. On 24 November, it did. The November 2026 core update finished that morning. It began on 10 November at 10:06 US/Pacific and ended on 24 November at 6:03 US/Pacific — close to 14 days. The Search Status Dashboard entry reads: "The rollout was complete as of November 24, 2026." About an hour later, Google opened a new entry on the same dashboard. It was not a rollout. It was a notice: the December 2026 core update, preannounced. Google has always announced core updates on the day they start. This is the first time it has given advance warning of one. The notice is short.

articles.body: Project Ensemble, 토큰화 결제의 실험이 보여주는 것. 이 주제는 내 시선을 단번에 사로잡는다. 중앙은행과 금융기관들이 돈의 미래를 놓고 씨름하는 중요한 실험들을 보여주기 때문이다. 이 분야가 30년간 진화하는 것을 지켜보며, 나는 수많은 개념 증명과 시범 프로그램을 목격했다. 지금 진정으로 눈에 띄는 것은 기술 그 자체만이 아니다. 시스템 비효율성을 해결하려는 협력적인 정신, 그것도 국경을 넘나드는 협력이다. 하지만 이 분석에 앞서 중요한 전제 하나를 깔아둔다. 'Project Ensemble' 자체의 구체적인 세부 사항, 결과, 참여자 등은 이 글의 자료에서 제공되지 않았다. 그러니 여기서 제시하는 통찰은 특정 프로젝트의 사실에 대한 직접적인 보고가 아니다. 대신, 토큰화 결제 분야에서 유사한 이니셔티브들에 대한 폭넓고 전문적인 이해에서 비롯된 것이다. 나는 Project Ensemble과 같은, 토큰화 결제에 초점을 맞춘 프로젝트가 무엇을 보여줄지 논의할 것이다. 중앙은행과 국제기구가 공개적으로 기록한 노력들에서 유사점과 교훈을 끌어낼 것이다. 내 관점은 이렇다. 이 실험들은 단순히 효율성만을 위한 것이 아니다. 글로벌 금융의 근본적인 틀을 재정의하는 작업이다. 성공 여부는 암호화 기술의 영리함보다는 상호운용성과 법적 명확성에 달려 있다. 앞으로 12-24개월 안에 이 두 가지 측면에서 실질적인 진전이 없다면, 많은 유망한 시범 프로그램들은 그저 시범 단계에 머무를 뿐이다. 서론 토큰화 결제 이야기를 꺼내면, 대중의 담론은 소매용 중앙은행 디지털 화폐(CBDC)로 쉽게 쏠리기 마련이다.

articles.title: Python json.dumps ensure_ascii Made My Claude Prompts 2.3x Bigger
articles.excerpt: A 20-minute Korean voice session should cost about the same to score as a 20-minute English one. Mine cost more than twice as much, and for three months I assumed that was just "how Korean tokenizes."…
articles.body: A 20-minute Korean voice session should cost about the same to score as a 20-minute English one. Mine cost more than twice as much, and for three months I assumed that was just "how Korean tokenizes." It wasn't. It was one default argument: json.dumps with ensure_ascii=True . Every Hangul syllable in my transcripts was reaching Claude as a six-character \uXXXX escape, and I was paying for every one of those characters as tokens. This post is the autopsy: how I found it, what I measured across 500 replayed scoring calls, and the two smaller bugs the fix caused. TL;DR Python's json.dumps defaults to ensure_ascii=True , which rewrites every non-ASCII character as \uXXXX . One Korean syllable becomes 6 ASCII characters.

articles.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
articles.excerpt: From Tomb Raider to Silent Hill, eight classic PlayStation games whose tank controls, cameras, or lost code make them hard to play today
articles.body: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.

articles.title: Dropping missiles from orbit? 2 European companies sign agreement to study the idea
articles.excerpt: Atmos Space Cargo will fly its first Phoenix cargo-return capsule on SpaceX's Bandwagon 3 rideshare mission, which is scheduled to launch this spring.
articles.body: A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit. Atmos, a space company known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle , will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project. "We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, said in a statement on Nov. 18. The system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies said that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.
